Rashi on Menachot 90a:10:1.hebrew: רבי עקיבא סבר מדת יבש לא נמשחה כל עיקר - וחול היא, לפיכך מה שבפנים בכלי קדושת פה הוא דמקדש ליה, הילכך מה דאיצטריך ליה מקדש, בירוצין דלא צריך ליה לא מקדש, לפיכך בירוציהן חול:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:10:1.english: Rabbi Akiva holds that the measure for dry goods was never anointed at all - and it is non-sacred; therefore, what is inside the vessel is consecrated by the sanctity of its designated fill line, and so whatever amount is needed is consecrated, while the overflow, which is not needed, is not consecrated. Therefore, their overflow is non-sacred.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:11:1.english: This is the reason - that the liquid measure's overflow is sacred: because its overflow was uprooted from within the vessel.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:11:2.english: And it comes from the body of the vessel - [It comes] from the sacred [vessel]; therefore it is sacred.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:12:1.hebrew: למאי דצריך - למה שבתוך הכלי איכוין למיקדש, ולא לבירוצין, ואמאי מיקדשי הבירוצין:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:12:1.english: "That which he requires" - He intends to consecrate only what is inside the vessel, and not the overflow; so why should the overflow become consecrated?

Rashi on Menachot 90a:13:1.english: 'Not knowingly' - even though he did not intend to consecrate the overflow, the sacred vessels (vessels of service) sanctify it regardless.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:13:2.hebrew: גזירה שמא יאמרו - דמאן דחזי דהנך בירוצין לא קדשי, אע"ג דאתו מגוויה דמנא, אמרי הכי נמי מוציאין מכלי שרת לחול. אבל יבש, דלא אתי מגופיה דמנא, לא אתו למימר ביה מוציאין מכלי שרת לחול:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:13:2.english: A decree lest they say - For one who sees that these overflows are not consecrated, even though they come from inside the vessel, will say the same of it: that [substances] may be taken from a service vessel to non-sacred use. But dry [flour], which does not come from the body of the vessel, they will not come to say of it that [substances] may be taken from a service vessel to non-sacred use.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:14:1.english: He arranged the bread and the bowls after Shabbat - Not in accordance with its commandment, for its commandment was to arrange it on Shabbat.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:14:2.english: Invalid - Because the bread must remain on the table for two Sabbaths.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:14:3.english: How should he do it - So that the bread and the bowls should be valid.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:14:4.hebrew: יניחנו - שלא יקטיר הבזיכין ולא יסלק הלחם עד לשבת שניה הבאה, ונמצא הלחם והבזיכין על השולחן ט"ו ימים ושני ימי שבת. שאפילו הוא על השולחן אותן ז' ימים שעד לשבת יותר מדינו, אין בכך כלום. הכא נמי ניגזור שלא יניחנו לשבת הבאה, שמא יאמרו כשם שאלו אין נפסלין אע"פ ששהו שם יותר מדינן, כך מפקידים בכלי שרת כל זמן שרוצה ואין נפסל בלינה:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:14:4.english: Let him leave it - [That is, the concern is] lest he not burn the frankincense bowls and not remove the bread until the following second Sabbath, and the bread and the frankincense bowls would thus end up sitting on the Table for fifteen days and two Sabbaths. For even though [in the case under discussion] it sits on the Table those seven days until the [next] Sabbath longer than it is supposed to, this is of no consequence. Here too, then, we should decree that he may not leave it until the coming Sabbath - lest people say: just as these [loaves] are not disqualified even though they remained there longer than prescribed, so too one may leave [sanctified items] deposited in a service vessel for as long as one wishes, and they will not be disqualified by overnight exposure.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:16:1.hebrew: פנים - לחם הפנים, דהוא בהיכל, אמדות קרמית שהן חוץ בעזרה:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:16:1.english: Inside - [This refers to] the showbread, which is in the Sanctuary; whereas the Kramit measures are outside in the [Temple] Courtyard.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:16:2.hebrew: פנים לאו כ"ע ידעי - שכן אירע בזה הלחם אלא הכהנים, וכהנים ידעי טעמא דמילתא, דכהנים זריזין וליכא למיגזר:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:16:2.english: The interior is not known to everyone - for this [matter of] the showbread occurs only [in the presence of] the priests, and priests know the rationale of the matter - that priests are zealous - and there is no [need] to decree [a safeguard].

Rashi on Menachot 90a:16:3.english: Outside, everyone knows - And there is [reason] to decree lest they say, etc.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:17:1.english: To supplement the altar - That they purchase burnt offerings with them and thereby keep the altar occupied when there are no [other] sacrifices there, so that the altar should not stand idle.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:19:1.english: One who undertook to supply fine flour - That he received money from the Temple treasurer in order to supply fine flour all year, and he undertook to give four se'ah per sela, but [the price] rose.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:19:2.english: And three se'ah stood [at the price of] a sela - He gives four se'ah, just as he received [them].

Rashi on Menachot 90a:1:1.english: IS THERE A VOLUNTARY GUILT-OFFERING? — Hence, it may be sacrificed on the altar only together with its libations.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:3:1.english: Its heaping was within it - [The Kohen Gadol's measuring vessel] was so large that when it was leveled off, it already held a full tenth [of an ephah].

Rashi on Menachot 90a:4:1.english: "For the measure of dry goods, their overflow is non-sacred" - What falls from the vessel after it has been filled, that is the "overflow" (birutzin).

Rashi on Menachot 90a:5:1.hebrew: אלא שהלח נעקר - שהבירוצין נכנסו בכלי ונתקדשו בו, ושוב נעקרו ממנו כשנפלו חוץ, לפיכך הן קדש, דנכנסו בכלי ונתקדשו בו:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:5:1.english: Rather, [it is] that the liquid was displaced - The overflow had entered the vessel and become consecrated there, and was then displaced from it when it spilled outside; therefore it is sacred, since it had entered the vessel and become consecrated in it.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:5:2.hebrew: ובירוצין של יבש אינו נעקר - מתוכו של כלי, שלא נכנס בתוך הכלי ולא נתקדש בו, לפיכך הוא חול:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:5:2.english: AND THE OVERFLOW OF DRY [MEASURES] IS NOT DISPLACED - from within the vessel; that is, [the dry overflow] never entered into the vessel and was never consecrated in it, and therefore it is non-sacred.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:6:1.english: Whose [opinion is this] - This is referring to that which is taught [in the mishna]: All the measures were heaped.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:6:2.english: IF [the mishna follows] RABBI MEIR — Since he stated above (Menachot 87a) that the heaped vessel, with which one measured the flour for all the other meal-offerings, [was different from] the level vessel that was the measure of the High Priest, which was so much larger that the amount that filled the [smaller] vessel when heaped would fill this one only to the level line.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:6:3.english: AND IT WAS LEVELED - meaning, there was not even one heaped measure at all.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:7:1.hebrew: ומאי כל מדות - דלא תימא כל המדות שהיו שם היו גדושות, דלא היתה אלא אחת גדושה:
Rashi on Menachot 90a:7:1.english: And what [does the mishna mean by] "all measures" - Do not say that all the measuring-vessels that were there were heaped, for there was only one that was heaped.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:7:2.english: Rather, this is what the mishna is teaching: All measurements [kol medidot] - the measurements that they took with it were heaped.

Rashi on Menachot 90a:9:1.english: They were not anointed on the outside - Therefore, their overflow is non-sacred.

Tosafot on Menachot 90a:14:1.hebrew: כיצד יעשה - שלא יבא דבר לפסול, יניחנה עם הבזיכין לשבת הבאה. אי נמי, מה יעשה מן הלחם אחר שהוקטרו הבזיכין:
Tosafot on Menachot 90a:14:1.english: How should he act - So that nothing should come to disqualify it, he should leave it together with the frankincense bowls [to remain] for the coming Sabbath. Alternatively, [the question is:] what should he do with the bread after the frankincense bowls have been burned?

Tosafot on Menachot 90a:14:2.hebrew: שאפילו הוא על השולחן ימים [רבים] אין בכך כלום - תימה, דבפרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פז.) בעא מיניה רבא מרבה: לינה מועלת בראשו של מזבח או אינה מועלת? היכי דמי? אי דלא ירדו, השתא לנו בעזרה אמרת לא ירדו, בראשו של מזבח מיבעיא? אלא דירדו. לשולחן מדמינן לה, דתנן: שאפי' הוא על השולחן ימים [רבים] אין בכך כלום. והשתא הא לא דמי לשולחן, דהא אסידרו באחד בשבת קאי, משום דכלי שרת אין מקדשין שלא בזמנן, כדמוכח בפרק שתי הלחם (לקמן מנחות ד' ק.) דדייקינן מהכא: ואי ס"ד כלי שרת מקדשין שלא בזמנן, ליקדוש וליפסל. ואם סידרן בשבת, הכי נמי דאם לא סילקן לשבת אחרת היה נפסל בלינה. ואהך גופה דאחד בשבת מקשי התם: דאי לילה אין מחוסר זמן, כי מטי לילה דבי שימשי תיקדוש ותיפסל! ומשני רבא: בשקדם וסילקו. ורב אשי משני: אפילו בשלא קדם וסילקו, נעשה כמי שסידרו הקוף. וא"כ גבי מזבח, אפילו מדמית ליה לשולחן נמי תועיל בו לינה. וי"ל דלשון "שאפי' הוא על השולחן" משמע ליה נתינת טעם אההוא דסידרו אחר השבת, דלכך לא חיישינן עליה, משום דבכל לחם הפנים כמו הנסדר בזמנו, אפילו הוא על השולחן ימים [רבים] אין בכך כלום. ומיהו על כרחין לאו טעם גמור הוא, דהכא היינו טעמא משום דכלי שרת אין מקדשין אלא בזמנן:
Tosafot on Menachot 90a:14:2.english: That even if it remains on the Table for many days, it does not matter - This is difficult: for in the chapter "The Altar Sanctifies" (Zevahim 87a), Rava asked Rabbah: does overnight stay take effect on top of the Altar, or does it not take effect? What are the circumstances? If the [sacrificial parts] had not come down [from the Altar], then since we said they may not remain overnight in the Azarah [courtyard], is it even necessary to ask about the top of the Altar [which is more stringent]? Rather, [the case is] where they had come down. And he compared it to the Table, since the Mishnah teaches: even if it remains on the Table for many days, it does not matter. But now, [the top of the Altar] is really not comparable to the Table, for [the reason the Table bread is not disqualified] is based on the arrangement that takes place on Shabbat — because service vessels do not sanctify outside their proper time, as is proven in the chapter of the Two Loaves (below, Menachot 100a), where we derive from here: if you should think that service vessels do sanctify outside their proper time, let it become sanctified and thereby disqualified [by overnight stay]! And if one arranged [the loaves] on Shabbat, then likewise — if he did not remove them by the following Shabbat, they would be disqualified by overnight stay. And on that very point — [the arrangement on] Shabbat — the Gemara there asks: if nightfall is not a deficiency of time [for the bread's disqualification], then when Friday night arrives, let it become sanctified and thereby disqualified! Rava answers: [the case is] where he preceded [Friday night] and removed it [before nightfall]. And Rav Ashi answers: even where he did not precede and remove it, it is treated as though a monkey had arranged it [i.e., it was never sanctified at all]. If so, regarding the Altar — even if you compare it to the Table, overnight stay should take effect on it [since the Altar, unlike the Table, does sanctify in real time]. One may answer: the language "even if it remains on the Table" is understood [by Rava] as providing the reason for [the leniency regarding] bread arranged after Shabbat — that is why we have no concern about it: because all showbread, like that arranged in its proper time, even if it remains on the Table for many days, does not matter. However, one is compelled to say that this is not a complete reason [for that leniency], for the real reason here is that service vessels do not sanctify except at their proper time.

Tosafot on Menachot 90a:19:1.hebrew: בירוצי מדות - אע״ג דנתקדשו, לוקחין מהן כבשים לעולות קייץ, כדפרישית בריש פירקין (מנחות דף פח.) דלב ב״ד מתנה עליהם:
Tosafot on Menachot 90a:19:1.english: Overflows of the measures - Even though they became consecrated, one purchases lambs from them for the burnt-offerings of kayitz ha-mizbe'aḥ, as I explained at the beginning of this chapter (Menachot 88a), for the heart of the court stipulates conditions upon them.
